MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MAY 15, 2023

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:04 p.m. at the George F Canyon Nature Center, 27305
  Palos Verdes Dr. E., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth
  McCormick, and Bain (arrived at 6:19 p.m.)

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 17,
  2023

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  POPE to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  APRIL 17, 2023.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  EQUESTRIAN FEES REVIEW

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
May 15, 2023
   Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked how the City would enforce the categories
  of the horse trainers. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the trainers would self-
  police themselves and that he is very familiar with many of the trainers and what
  their approved categories are.

  Superintendent Goldsmith and Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the City does not
  track use of the arenas by the trainers or keep records of the percentage of revenue
  collected by trainers compared to the cost to maintain the arenas, in response to
  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the arenas are also used by the public which would
  make it difficult to breakdown maintenance costs by just the horse trainers at the
  arenas. She also noted that the City added a city property use fee to trainer permits
  to account for some of the maintenance costs, in response to VICE CHAIR
  MCCORMICK.

  Supervisor Pinuelas also noted that as an equestrian city, the City wants people to
  come learn and use the arenas for training, in response to VICE CHAIR
  MCCORMICK.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that this is the main form of business for most of
  the City approved trainers and that they use the arenas about 30-40 hours a week,
  in response to VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted that it now costs a lot of money to board a
  horse at a private boarding facility. She also noted that the cost of feed has gone
  up at the local feed markets which establishes the market price of the individual
  fees the horse trainers charge.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that it was difficult for the City to find comparisons for
  trainer fees from other City’s that have public arenas, in response to VICE CHAIR
  MCCORMICK. Superintendent Goldsmith noted that other cities may have bridle
  trails, but he was not aware of other cities having public arenas, in response to
  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK and COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  TO APPROVE STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION OF FY 23-24 EQUESTRIAN
  FEES AND CHARGES.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
May 15, 2023
   AYES:  Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth, McCormick
  ABSENT:  Bain

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  2023 SUMMER MOVIE NIGHT UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the 2023 Summer Movie Nights
  including the location, time, and movie selections. He noted the rescheduled date
  of the first movie night from June 10 to June 17.

  B.  MAYOR’S RIDE DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief overview of the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride held
  on Saturday, May 13. He stated that the ride went well with a good turnout from
  local dignitaries and the public. He also noted that everyone was excited that the
  local Scouts returned to provide their Pancake Breakfast, serving an estimated 700
  people throughout the morning.

  C.  PV STREET FAIR & MUSIC FESTIVAL PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOOTH
  SHIFTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the booth shifts for the upcoming
  PV Street Fair and Music Festival. She stated that Commissioners could email
  Coordinator Morrow if they were interested in volunteering their time during one of
  the booth shifts.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the booth provides outreach for City events and
  Pepper Tree Foundation information, in response to VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  COMMISSIONER POPE encouraged other commissioners to volunteer for a booth
  shift at the street fair, explaining and how it is a great way to promote the City’s
  programs and activities since it is a large-scale community event.

  D.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK stated that the group of dog owners with approximately
  20 unleashed dogs off leash continues to meet at Highridge Park on Thursday

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
May 15, 2023
   afternoons. He noted that one of the dogs ran over to him aggressively and
  attempted to attack his dog while he was walking around the park.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if there were more trash cans needed
  around the baseball fields at Ernie Howlett Park. Superintendent Goldsmith stated
  that Waste Management missed the trash cans located at the field during their
  routine trash pickup at the park over a couple of weeks causing the overflow. He
  noted Maintenance staff emptied the trash cans in that area and that he coordinated
  with Waste Management to routinely check that area on pick-up days.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked a follow up question regarding the unleashed
  dogs at Highridge Park previously mentioned by VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK. She
  asked what the proper procedure would be for a resident to report that to someone.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated it would be best to first notify the Sheriff’s
  Department if present at the park during the activity. He also stated that Staff will
  send code compliance staff to Highridge Park to attempt to deter this activity from
  occurring in the future.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF APRIL 11, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF APRIL 25, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  COMMISSIONER POPE congratulated the Commission for the selection of their
  proposed name, Founders Park, being adopted by the City Council.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PUBLIC PARK OUTREACH

  NONE.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER AND PRESERVE/TRAIL,
  DAPPLEGRAY PARK, FOUNDERS PARK AND TABER GROVE

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
May 15, 2023
   Supervisor Pinuelas gave an overview of the proposed and approved renovations
  of the George F Canyon Nature Center and presented a diagram of the new
  renderings of the exterior and interior of the design. She stated that the Pepper Tree
  Fundraising Committee is developing a fundraising campaign for the Nature Center
  project.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked about the QR code on the diagram and if it
  was for the donations being requested by the fundraising subcommittee. Supervisor
  Pinuelas confirmed that the QR code would send a person straight to the donation
  page. COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked if someone could make a monthly
  donation compared to just a one-time donation. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that an
  endowment donation program is being planned but has not been set up yet.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if there was going to be an option to purchase a
  plaque or sponsor a tree around the new nature center. Supervisor Pinuelas stated
  that the fundraising subcommittee has discussed purchasing a display with metal
  leaves that would be placed on a wall but that those plans are still being finalized.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the plans are to have a limit of 40 to 60 parking
  spaces, in response to COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA.

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave an overview of the development of Founders Park and
  stated the bid process was open. She added the bids would be reviewed at the
  June City Council meeting for awarding of the contract. She also mentioned the
  proposed dates for the completion of the project.

  Supervisor Pinuelas introduced Holly Gray, Education Director for the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC), who gave a brief overview of the PVPLC
  2022 Annual Report and activities and programs occurring at the George F Canyon
  Nature Center and Preserve/Trail.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the Family Nature Club program. Ms. Gray
  stated that the program started in early 2020 and was shut down due to COVID.
  The program was then brought back as a virtual program which is reflected in the
  numbers in the annual report. She noted that they have not been able to bring back
  the 2020 version of the in-person program. She stated that a new version of the
  nature club program was brought back recently with the graduates of the student
  naturalist program and that they were able to bring their families as well.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the volunteers for maintenance of the trail
  and if that program was going to return. Ms. Gray stated that they have tested out
  bringing the volunteer days back, but that they have not had the staff available.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
May 15, 2023
   Ms. Gray stated that the annual report doesn’t capture the volunteers that are
  currently assisting as they do have interns and high school assistants and that they
  have also started a high school volunteer internship program, in response to
  COMMISSIONER POPE.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked how they track the numbers listed in the annual
  report. Ms. Gray stated there is an online RSVP sign-in process for the activities
  and programs. She noted that staff keeps a tally sheet as patrons enter the Nature
  Center, but that staff does not keep track of the patrons that use the trails.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked if staff tracked whether the visitors are
  residents or non-residents and if staff collects e-mail addresses during any of the
  program participant sign ups to assist with follow ups regarding future events or
  donations. Ms. Gray noted that they have an online RSVP sign-up system for their
  hike and program participants during which participants provide their email
  addresses.

  Ms. Gray stated there are QR codes that offer trail maps along the trails but no
  other information is provided, in response to VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  **COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH LEFT THE MEETING AT 6:55 PM**

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION COMPLETED A BRIEF TOUR OF THE
  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER AND THEN PROCEEDED TO
  DAPPLEGRAY PARK FOR A TOUR**

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that more sand would be added to the arenas as
  part of the routine replenishment and that staff replaced the main park sign. He also
  noted that he would like to have more mounting blocks made and shared that he is
  looking for any local scouts interested in building some as a scout project.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION DECIDED NOT TO TOUR THE GEORGE
  F CANYON PRESERVE/TRAIL DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF POISON OAK
  ALONG THE TRAIL. THEY ALSO DECIDED TO NOT TOUR THE FUTURE SITE
  OF FOUNDERS PARK AND PROCEEDED TO TABOR GROVE FOR A TOUR**

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:26 PM TO THE
  NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JUNE 20, 2023, AT
  6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
May 15, 2023
   Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Judy Bain
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
May 15, 2023
